newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek court tries farmer for death of Moslem MP.
newsitem.headline: Greek court tries farmer for death of Moslem MP.

text.p: A Greek court opened the trial on Thursday of a farmer accused of manslaughter over the car-crash death of Greek Moslem deputy Sadik Ahmet in 1995, court officials said.
The trial of farmer Stelios Bletsis started in the northern city of Salonika and was expected to last around a week, the officials said.
Police said Ahmet's car and the farmer's tractor collided in July 1995. The deputy was killed and his wife and two children were injured.
Ahmet was elected to parliament in June 1989 and again in April 1990 as a representative of the Moslem minority in the northern Greek region of Thrace.
Ahmet had often angered Greek authorities for speaking out in parliament on behalf of what he described as a Turkish minority.

The Greek government says the country has no such thing as an ethnic Turkish minority but that there is a 130,000-strong Moslem community of various ethnic backgrounds, remnants of the Ottoman empire which ruled Western Thrace until 1913.
Turkey insists they are Turks and that their minority rights are violated by the Greek government.
